events.title: Women's March on Versailles
events.description: Angered by the high price and scarcity of bread, thousands of Parisian women and their allies marched to the royal palace at Versailles to confront the monarchy.
events.significance: The march forced the royal family to move to Paris and became a turning point in the French Revolution, weakening the king's authority.

events.title: First televised presidential address from the White House
events.description: President Harry S. Truman asked Americans to cut back on their grain consumption to help feed a Europe still recovering from World War II. He made the appeal in the first presidential speech broadcast on television.
events.significance: The address showed how television could carry a president's voice straight into American homes, and it changed how leaders speak to the public.

events.title: Monty Python's Flying Circus debuts
events.description: The BBC aired the first episode of the sketch comedy series created by the Monty Python troupe.
events.significance: The show's surreal, irreverent humor reshaped comedy worldwide and influenced generations of writers and performers.

events.title: Space Shuttle Challenger launches STS-41-G
events.description: Marc Garneau flew as a payload specialist on the mission, becoming the first Canadian in space. The crew also included Sally Ride and Kathryn Sullivan, the first time two women flew on the same space mission.
events.significance: The flight marked a milestone for Canada's space program and for women in spaceflight.

events.title: Bulldozer Revolution in Belgrade
events.description: Hundreds of thousands of protesters gathered in Belgrade to challenge the results of a disputed election. The crowds set fire to the Parliament building, and Slobodan Milosevic resigned two days later.
events.significance: The largely peaceful uprising ended Milosevic's rule over Yugoslavia and opened the way for democratic change in Serbia.
